newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 29.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:

* President Clinton acknowledged that Eugene Ludwig, the nation's senior banking regulator, should not have been included in a White House coffee for bankers that Clinton hosted and that the Democratic National Committee organized.
* President Clinton said he would not rule out higher Medicare premiums for the wealthy nor deeper cuts in the capital gains tax in his negotiations with Congress for a balanced budget agreement.

* Federal Bureau of Investigations officials interviewed by the Justice Department's inspector general say dozens of cases have been affected by problems with work done by the FBI's forensic laboratory.
* The New York State Senate voted 41-19 to reject a constitutional amendment to legalize casino gambling, a move that effectively kills the proposal until 1999.
* South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission says former policemen have confessed to killing Steve Biko and to other murders and are now filing amnesty applications.
* Jurors in the O.J. Simpson civil case begin deliberations to determine whether the former football star is responsible for the deaths of his ex-wife and Ronald Goldman.
* Robert Boyle, the chief executive of New York City's Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, is named as the head of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.
